title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a 'figure' is a pair (S,T) consisting of a set and a topology. The previous page has in mind essentially Alexandrov-type topologies, encoded by their specialisation preorder. Pages 37–38 define three order relations between figures.

- Sub-figure: S' is closed in S and carries the induced topology.
- (S',T') ≪ (S,T): S' ⊂ S and the inclusion is continuous.
- (S',T') ≼ (S,T), the new relation on this page: S' = S and T' is finer than T, i.e. id: (S,T') → (S,T) is continuous.

Grothendieck then returns to a 'situation C'. A sub-figure C ⊂ F is given, together with a refinement G' ≼ C. Put T = |C| and S = |F|. Then T is closed in (S,τ), τ0 is the topology induced on T, and τ0' is a finer topology on T. The problem is to find all refinements F' ≼ F inducing G' on C. These are the topologies τ' on S such that:
1. τ' is finer than τ, i.e. (S,τ') → (S,τ) is continuous; and
2. (T,τ0') → (S,τ') is continuous, indeed an embedding inducing τ0'.

He remarks that this is a 'mixed' situation, of initial type on the right and final type on the left. Concretely he needs:
- every τ-closed A ⊂ S to be τ'-closed;
- for every τ'-closed A', the trace A' ∩ T to be τ0'-closed.
He notes that T, being τ-closed, is τ'-closed, so the τ0'-closed subsets of T must themselves be τ'-closed in S.

The next page completes the argument. The sets A ∪ B, with A τ-closed and B ⊂ T τ0'-closed, are stable under finite unions. They are also stable under arbitrary intersections, by distributivity: ∩(A_i ∪ B_i) = ∪_J (∩_J A_i ∩ ∩_{I∖J} B_j). So they are the closed sets of a topology τ'. This τ' induces τ0' on T and τ on the open complement S∖T. It is the coarsest refinement of τ inducing τ0' on the closed piece T. Equivalently, it is the topology generated by τ together with the closed subspace topology τ0', or an initial topology for id_S and a collapse map onto T. In preorder terms this amounts to modifying the specialisation preorder on a closed (down-/up-closed) part.

The left margin describes infima ∧(S_i,T_i) via initial topologies on products and the associated preorder (x ≤ y iff f_i(x) ≤ f_i(y) for all i), and relates them to induced structures. This is elementary general topology serving the construction of an 'algebra of figures', i.e. lattice operations on topologized sets.
errors: Condition 2° as first written (continuity of T → (S,τ')) is weaker than what is wanted: one needs τ'|T = τ0'. Grothendieck corrects for this in the inserted remark (τ0' = τ'|T, T τ'-closed).
The marking τ'≤τ for 'finer' is an idiosyncratic convention, the opposite of the usual one in some texts. It is not an error, but should be noted.
In the bullet (ii) of the page the quantifier is garbled; the construction is completed only on the next page, where a converse is attempted and then struck out.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary point-set topology worked out as a lemma for the 'algèbre des figures'. The construction is correct and standard, and contains nothing that a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Below 'C ⊂ F' the symbol is a vertically rotated ≼ (i.e. G' ≼ C), not '∩'.
Under T the topology label appears to be τ0 with a small superscript (possibly 't'), not a question mark.
The struck-out word before 'T ↪ S' looks like a crossed-out start such as 'Comme', not dots.
In (i) 'A∈𝔉_τ(S)': the image shows a script F (closed sets for τ), consistent with the transcription.

Line (ii) reads roughly 'que pour [tout] A' fermé pour τ', i^{-1}(A') = A'∩T [soit] fermé pour τ0'' and continues on the next line 'soit fermé pour τ0'. Si fermé pour τ, τ0' = τ'|T, T étant fermé pour τ donc pour τ'. Les parties fermées de T pour τ0' sont fermées'.
